subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Network Effects and Lock-In
description: A quick, practical guide to Network Effects and Lock-In.

hook.text: You want to leave Facebook, but all your family photos, groups, and friends are there. You stay.

buildup.text: Network effects make platforms more valuable as more people join. Leaving means losing your connections.

discovery.text: Your data — photos, messages, friendships — becomes trapped on the platform, creating switching costs.

twist.text: Data portability rights exist in theory. In practice, exporting your data gives you files nobody else can read.

climax.text: Social media traps you with your own data. The more you share, the harder it is to leave.

punchline.text: Your data keeps you locked in. By design.

quiz.question: Why is it hard for users to leave social media platforms?
options: Network effects and data lock-in create high switching costs
